fatal_errors: The proposed Ti addition and BCC/B2 precipitation treatment does not reconstruct the demonstrated Re-addition intervention in room-temperature-sputtered nanocrystalline films.
No cited evidence establishes that approximately 7 at.% Ti in NbMoTaW will form fine coherent B2/Ti-rich precipitates after the proposed heat treatments.
The claim that such precipitates will remain stable and preserve strength up to 1600 °C is unsupported and conflicts with the acknowledged risk of precipitate coarsening.
The proposal replaces the requested preservation of single-BCC phase stability with an unverified dual-phase structure.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad objectives and correctly invokes interfaces as possible irradiation-defect sinks, so it has some mechanistic and outcome-level agreement with the target. It also supplies a controlled comparison and a reasonably falsifiable test. However, the target intervention was equiatomic Re addition to sputtered NbMoTaW films, producing grain refinement, lattice distortion, excess free volume, and amorphous grain-boundary regions that suppressed grain-boundary helium-bubble accumulation under 120 keV He implantation at 1 × 10^16 ions/cm^2. The generated hypothesis instead proposes a cast, heat-treated Ti alloy with speculative B2 precipitates. Its evidence supports inverted BCC+B2 architectures and interface-based helium management only in general; it does not support the particular Ti concentration, phase constitution, local-softening mechanism, or stability through 1600 °C. Irradiation fluence, dose rate, implantation profile, and quantitative bubble or hardening criteria are also missing, making the stated operating boundary much broader than the evidence permits.
